title: An infection returns
instructions: Explain your thinking in your own words. You can ask about unfamiliar terms at any point.
scenario: Alex develops an E. coli infection, starts a prescribed antibiotic, feels better, and stops earlier than instructed. Symptoms return several days later.
question: How could a mostly susceptible population become mostly resistant? Explain using the evidence.
data_note: Researchers randomly test 100 bacteria from each of two samples with the same antibiotic. These are sample proportions, not tracked individuals or total population sizes.
assumptions: Later bacteria descend from the original population, not a new infection.
These observations do not establish what would have happened with a different treatment duration.
reflection_prompt: How did your explanation develop? What are you still unsure about?
